scope: Nine implementation-family reviews. Evidence identifies scenarios, owners and tests, not an exhaustive line-by-line audit. Board-specific code is excluded; unchanged shared files may contain board wiring.

groups.scenario: Build requests and consume successful/rejected streams for OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic clients.
groups.reason: Keep typed client dispatch and provider-specific authentication/parameters. The generic request and collector already own common behavior. Correct the provider-specific failure label in their shared caller.
validation: Local HTTP/SSE contract checks cover both wire formats, auth, max_tokens, tool advertisement, tool-call decoding, usage and non-retried 401 failures. No live provider was contacted.

groups.scenario: Cancel, retry a rejected request, restore history and use deterministic fallback.
groups.reason: Keep one retry classifier and durable-output cutoff for both providers. Canonical history and clearing projection remain distinct; fallback has no network span. Do not replace these differences with a common transport abstraction.
validation: Existing retry pacing, cancellation, durable-output, clearing and history tests pass. Adapter failure tests check request-span closure without committed output.

groups.scenario: Resolve a displayed human approval or an exact automatic candidate.
groups.reason: Share dispatch only after each entry point checks its own evidence. Preserve approval source, kind, exact candidate checks, started/finished guards and forwarding behavior.
validation: New parity regression checks actual writes, occurrence identity, event order, changed automatic candidates and duplicate decisions. Existing bash/domain/filesystem approval and retry checks pass.

groups.scenario: Run sync or async tools, refuse a grant, retry a contained attempt and handle late completion.
groups.reason: Sync results and async Started outcomes have different owners/timing. Keep live-occurrence correlation, session-owned turn completion, original results on refused retries and grant revalidation before effects. Board arms remain excluded.
validation: Full default suite covers real agentd execution, approved contained Git writes, grant retries and stale completion handling.

groups.scenario: Wrap a command for Linux supervision, macOS Seatbelt or Linux unit tests.
groups.reason: One preparation function owns cwd, explicit environment overrides/removals, scratch TMPDIR and stdin/stdout/stderr. Keep wrapper argv, policy installation, process-group creation and pre_exec safety OS-local.
validation: New real-child test checks cwd, set/removed environment, scratch creation and all three streams. Default tests exercise the production Linux helper separately from cfg(test) spawning. macOS cross-check stopped in aws-lc-sys because the host C compiler lacks Darwin support; no macOS execution claimed.

groups.scenario: Read normal and sandboxed stdout/stderr through temporary interruptions.
groups.reason: Keep async tasks and blocking threads but share collection/termination rules. Retry Interrupted reads; EOF and permanent errors retain their prior stopping behavior. Process waiting and bounded drain remain with each execution path.
validation: A scripted reader drives both pumps through interruption before/after data, binary bytes, EOF and permanent error. Real timeout, partial output, spill, cwd and held-pipe tests pass.

groups.scenario: Cancel queued/running commands and terminate descendant processes.
groups.reason: Remove duplicate cfg-specific forwarding wrappers and the unused non-Unix group stub. Keep OS behavior in process.rs: Linux snapshots descendants before killing the process group; other Unix hosts use group termination. Non-Unix tree termination remains unimplemented, not a new platform guarantee.
validation: Linux tests cover setsid descendants, cancellation, queue ordering, panic cleanup and registry removal. No macOS/FreeBSD runtime or non-Unix runtime verification.

groups.scenario: Query containment support and interact with the OS primary selection.
groups.reason: Keep Linux/macOS capability checks distinct and unsupported sandbox spawning fail-closed. Primary selection is supported only on Linux/FreeBSD; absence elsewhere is intentional. Capture keeps Linux authenticated supervisor reports distinct from macOS best-effort denial-log collection.
validation: Linux default gate exercises supported containment. horizon-sandbox --all-targets cargo check for x86_64-unknown-freebsd passes; it verifies compilation of the unsupported-platform branch only, not execution or the entire application.

groups.scenario: Compile native host and WASM guest, share theme input and reload a real preview component.
groups.reason: Keep schema, registry and theme resolution shared; sockets, watcher, process-backed views and config publication remain native. Guest receipt/observer lifecycle is different from host publication. No board preview implementation was changed or selected for practical verification.
validation: Mandatory wasm32-wasip2 library check passes. The real preview component builds and the non-board theme/paint/reload ignored test passes in wasmtime. This is not a physical GUI, IME or platform clipboard test.
